title: Exam SC-500: Implementing End-to-End Security Controls for Cloud and AI Workloads

provenance.derivedFrom: https://learn.microsoft.com/credentials/certifications/resources/study-guides/sc-500 (page ms.date 2026-04-26, last updated 2026-07-31) — the published "Skills measured" section, transcribed one-to-one. Domain headings and area (H4) subheadings are taxonomy, recorded as published, same treatment as the CISSP outline's area labels.
provenance.areaLabels: Area ids/labels are the study guide's H4 subheadings under each domain (e.g. "Secure access to resources by using Microsoft Entra ID"), not the finer bullet list beneath them. The bullets are carried verbatim in each area's `tasks` array for classification grounding — Microsoft's own text: "The bullets that follow each of the skills measured are intended to illustrate how we are assessing that skill. Related topics may be covered in the exam."
provenance.weights: Domain weights are the published ranges (e.g. 20-25%), recorded as `weightMin`/`weightMax` plus a `weight` midpoint for sampler convenience. Confirm against the live study-guide page before trusting the midpoint for anything beyond rough sampling. Nothing in the coverage gate reads them.
provenance.correction: The exam's own scope, not the third-party practice-question bank: this exam is NOT "Microsoft Security Operations" — it is end-to-end security controls across identity, storage/DB/networking, compute (including AI workload security: Copilot, Entra Agent ID, Foundry guardrails), and security posture management. Domain 3 (Secure compute) devotes its first of three areas entirely to AI security.
